text: “Why are you always so full of answers?”“Because life’s so full of questions.”
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Why should he remember her? Why should she remember him? She had other things to think about. She was a grown woman. She had to face life. Even if all life had to show her was a locked door, and behind the locked door, no room.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: When we’ve agreed that something ought to be done, or not done, we get very stubborn. And when that meets up with another stubbornness, it can make a kind of war, a struggle of ideas, the only kind of war anybody ever wins.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: In the self-important, Falco reflected, there is always room for a little more self-importance.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Nobody had made this wilderness, and there was no evil in it and no good; it simply was.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: To know there is a choice is to have to make the choice: change or stay: river or rock.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: He always asked, why thus? why this way, not another way? I answered: Because in what we do daily and in the way we do it, we enact the gods. He said: Then the gods are only what we do. I said: In what we do rightly, the gods are.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: The old knowledge had been difficult but not distressing. It had been all paradox and myth, and it had made sense. The new knowledge was all fact and reason, and it made no sense.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: It may be in our sexuality that we are most easily enslaved, both men and women. It may be there, even as free men and women, that we find freedom hardest to keep. The politics of the flesh are the roots of power.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: I was utterly miserable, and yet fearless as I had never been. I was carefree. It was like dying. It would be foolish to worry about anything while one died.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: I can never get used to the fact, though I know it, that women are born cynics. Men have to learn cynicism. Infant girls could teach it to them.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Is it the gods who set this fire in our hearts, or do we each make our fierce desire into a god?
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: "Why must there be war?" "Oh Lavinia, what a woman's question that is! Because men are men."
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: They say Mars absolves the warrior from the crimes of war, but those who were not the warriors, those for whom the war was said to be fought, even though they never wanted it to be fought, who absolves them?
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Men are afraid of virgins, but they have a cure for their own fear and the virgin's virginity: fucking.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: There's a good deal in common between the mind's eye and the TV screen, and though the TV set has all too often been the boobtube, it could be, it can be, the box of dreams.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: The dance of renewal, the dance that made the world, was always danced here at the edge of things, on the brink, on the foggy coast.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Success is somebody else's failure. Success is the American Dream we can keep dreaming because most people in most places, including thirty million of ourselves, live wide awake in the terrible reality of poverty.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: The children of the revolution are always ungrateful, and the revolution must be grateful that it is so.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: We are volcanoes. When we women offer our experience as our truth, as human truth, all the maps change. There are new mountains.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: Reason is a faculty far larger than mere objective force. When either the political or the scientific discourse announces itself as the voice of reason, it is playing God, and should be spanked and stood in the corner.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: If science fiction is the mythology of modern technology, then its myth is tragic.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: If you want your writing to be taken seriously, don’t marry and have kids, and above all, don’t die. But if you have to die, commit suicide. They approve of that.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: The unread story is not a story; it is little black marks on wood pulp. The reader, reading it, makes it live: a live thing, a story.
author: Ursula K. Le Guin

text: The universe was a language with a perfectly ambiguous grammar. Every physical event was an utterance that could be parsed in two entirely different ways, one causal and the other teleological.
author: Ted Chiang
work: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)
ko: 우주는 완벽하게 중의적인 문법을 가진 언어였다. 모든 물리적 사건은 전혀 다른 두 방식으로 읽히는 발화였다. 하나는 인과로, 다른 하나는 목적으로.

text: God is not just, God is not kind, God is not merciful, and understanding that is essential to true devotion.
author: Ted Chiang
work: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)
ko: 신은 정의롭지 않고, 다정하지 않고, 자비롭지 않다. 그것을 이해하는 일이 참된 신앙의 핵심이다.

text: Just as seeing Heaven's light gave him an awareness of God's presence in all things in the mortal plane, so it has made him aware of God's absence in all things in Hell.
author: Ted Chiang
work: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)
ko: 천국의 빛을 본 일이 필멸의 세계 만물에 깃든 신의 존재를 깨닫게 했듯, 그것은 지옥의 만물에서 신의 부재를 깨닫게 했다.

text: That wouldn’t be maturity; it would be letting an expert system make your decisions for you. Maturity means seeing the differences, but realizing they don’t matter. There’s no technological shortcut.
author: Ted Chiang
work: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)
ko: 그건 성숙이 아니다. 전문가 시스템에게 결정을 맡기는 것일 뿐이다. 성숙이란 차이를 보되 그것이 중요하지 않음을 아는 것이다. 기술적 지름길은 없다.

text: We can’t avoid these images and still live in the modern world. And that means we can’t kick this habit, because beauty is a drug that you can’t abstain from unless you literally keep your eyes closed all the time.
author: Ted Chiang
work: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)

text: Technology is being used to manipulate us through our emotional reactions, so it’s only fair that we use it to protect ourselves too.
author: Ted Chiang
work: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002)
ko: 기술은 우리의 감정적 반응을 이용해 우리를 조종하는 데 쓰인다. 그렇다면 우리도 그것으로 스스로를 지키는 게 공평하다.

text: Four things do not come back: the spoken word, the sped arrow, the past life, and the neglected opportunity.
author: Ted Chiang
ko: 돌아오지 않는 네 가지가 있다. 내뱉은 말, 쏘아 버린 화살, 지나간 삶, 그리고 놓쳐 버린 기회.

text: The rewards will be purely intellectual, and over the long term, will that be enough?
author: Ted Chiang
ko: 보상은 순전히 지적인 것이다. 긴 시간을 두고 보면, 그것으로 충분할까?

text: For him, the keyboard and screen are a miserable substitute for being there, as unsatisfying as a jungle video game would be to a chimpanzee taken from the Congo.
author: Ted Chiang
ko: 그에게 키보드와 화면은 그곳에 있는 것의 초라한 대용품이다. 콩고에서 데려온 침팬지에게 정글 비디오게임이 그렇듯이.

text: Every quality that made a person more valuable than a database was a product of experience.
author: Ted Chiang
ko: 사람을 데이터베이스보다 가치 있게 만드는 모든 자질은 경험의 산물이었다.

text: When the public interest is involved, finding out what actually happened is important; justice is an essential part of the social contract, and you can’t have justice until you know the truth.
author: Ted Chiang
ko: 공익이 걸린 문제라면 실제로 무슨 일이 있었는지 밝히는 일이 중요하다. 정의는 사회계약의 핵심이고, 진실을 알기 전까지 정의는 없다.

text: Anyone who has wasted hours surfing the Internet knows that technology can encourage bad habits.
author: Ted Chiang
ko: 인터넷을 몇 시간씩 흘려보내 본 사람이라면 기술이 나쁜 습관을 부추긴다는 것을 안다.

text: But the church as an institution has always been able to derive strength from the evidence when it’s useful and ignore it when it’s not.
author: Ted Chiang

text: Even if humanity is not the reason for which the universe was made, I still wish to understand the way it operates. We human beings may not be the answer to the question why, but I will keep looking for the answer to how.
author: Ted Chiang

text: He was in no position to judge these people. So what if they felt sorry for themselves? Better to wallow in self-pity over nothing than to have actually screwed up your life.
author: Ted Chiang

text: Much of modern astronomy is promised on the Copernican principle, the idea that we are not at the center of the universe and are not observing it from a privileged position; this is pretty much the opposite of young-earth creationism.
author: Ted Chiang

text: The glories and obstacles of the past are just a speck compared to the vastness of the future.
author: Liu Cixin
ko: 과거의 영광과 장애물은 미래의 광대함에 비하면 티끌에 지나지 않는다.

text: A professor of philosophy once said that lesson one for freshman in his field should consist of a long, hard look late at night at the stars. I think this would be an even more apt first lesson for aspiring writers of sci-fi.
author: Liu Cixin

text: The cosmos had not chosen humanity after all. In the old timeline, humans had created the apex civilization on earth, but that had been a one-time and accidental chance. In our human conceit, we’d taken the accidental for the inevitable.
author: Liu Cixin

text: The products of modern science have already surpassed the wonders of magic.
author: Liu Cixin
ko: 현대 과학의 산물은 이미 마법의 경이를 넘어섰다.

text: It’s an interesting thing, really: The rigorous, science-based predictions of scientists and futurologists and the spirited “flights of fancy” of sci-fi writers are just about equally (in)accurate!
author: Liu Cixin

text: That humans will biologically alter themselves is inevitable, which makes life sciences the most terrifying of the sciences.
author: Liu Cixin
ko: 인간이 스스로를 생물학적으로 개조하리라는 것은 필연이다. 그래서 생명과학은 모든 과학 중 가장 두려운 것이 된다.

text: Quantitative change eventually gives way to qualitative change.
author: Liu Cixin
ko: 양적인 변화는 결국 질적인 변화에 자리를 내준다.

text: Exploring the secrets of the universe is the basic instinct of all intelligent life.
author: Liu Cixin
ko: 우주의 비밀을 탐사하는 일은 모든 지적 생명의 근본 본능이다.

text: Now I understand one of the important reasons for going to college and getting an education is to learn that the things you've believed in all your life aren't true, and that nothing is what it appears to be.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 대학에 가서 교육을 받는 중요한 이유 하나를 이제 알겠다. 평생 믿어 온 것들이 사실이 아니며, 무엇도 보이는 그대로가 아님을 배우는 것이다.

text: The answer can't be found in books — or be solved by bringing it to other people. Not unless you want to remain a child all your life. You've got to find the answer inside you — feel the right thing to do.
author: Daniel Keyes

text: My most absorbing interests at the present time are etymologies of ancient languages, the newer works on the calculus of variations, and Hindu history. It's amazing the way things, apparently disconnected, hang together.
author: Daniel Keyes

text: People resent being shown that they don't approach the complexities of the problem — they don't know what exists beyond the surface ripples.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 사람들은 자신이 문제의 복잡함에 미치지 못한다는 걸 보여 주면 불쾌해한다. 수면의 잔물결 너머에 무엇이 있는지 모르는 것이다.

text: Strange about learning; the farther I go the more I see that I never knew even existed.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 배움이란 이상하다. 멀리 갈수록, 존재하는 줄도 몰랐던 것들이 더 많이 보인다.

text: A child may not know how to feed itself, or what to eat, yet it knows hunger.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 아이는 스스로 먹는 법도, 무엇을 먹어야 하는지도 모를 수 있다. 그래도 배고픔은 안다.

text: The foolish thing was trying to solve the problem all by myself. But the deeper I get tangled up in this mass of dreams and memories the more I realize that emotional problems can't be solved as intellectual problems are.
author: Daniel Keyes

text: The meaning of my total existence involves knowing the possibilities of my future as well as my past, where I'm going as well as where I've been.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 내 존재 전체의 의미는 과거만이 아니라 미래의 가능성을, 어디에 있었는지만이 아니라 어디로 가는지를 아는 데 있다.

text: I am not only a thing, but also a way of being — one of many ways — and knowing the paths I have followed and the ones left to take will help me understand what I am becoming.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 나는 하나의 사물일 뿐 아니라 존재하는 하나의 방식이기도 하다. 수많은 방식 중 하나. 걸어온 길과 남은 길을 아는 일이 내가 무엇이 되어 가는지 이해하게 해 줄 것이다.

text: So many of the ideas on which our psychologists base their beliefs about human intelligence, memory, and learning are all wishful thinking.
author: Daniel Keyes

text: There are a lot of people who will give money or materials, but very few who will give time and affection.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 돈이나 물건을 주려는 사람은 많지만, 시간과 애정을 주려는 사람은 아주 적다.

text: How many great problems have gone unsolved because men didn't know enough, or have enough faith in the creative process and in themselves, to let go for the whole mind to work at it?
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 얼마나 많은 위대한 문제가 풀리지 못한 채 남았을까. 사람들이 충분히 알지 못해서, 혹은 창조의 과정과 자기 자신을 믿지 못해 정신 전체가 일하도록 놓아주지 못해서.

text: No one really starts anything new, Mrs Nemur. Everyone builds on other men's failures. There is nothing really original in science. What each man contributes to the sum of knowledge is what counts.
author: Daniel Keyes

text: We learn what something is not — and that is as important as a positive discovery to the man who is going to pick up from there. At least he knows what not to do.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 우리는 무엇이 아닌지를 배운다. 뒤이어 이어받을 사람에게는 그것도 긍정적인 발견만큼 중요하다. 적어도 하지 말아야 할 일은 알게 되니까.

text: I am afraid. Not of life, or death, or nothingness, but of wasting it as if I had never been.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 나는 두렵다. 삶도, 죽음도, 무(無)도 아니다. 애초에 존재한 적 없는 것처럼 그것을 낭비하는 일이 두렵다.

text: As when men to keep from being swept overboard in the storm clutch at each other's hands to resist being torn apart, so our bodies fused a link in the human chain that kept us from being swept into nothing.
author: Daniel Keyes

text: You don't know what it's like to have something happening inside you, that you can't see and can't control, and know it's all slipping through your fingers.
author: Daniel Keyes
ko: 안에서 무언가가 일어나는데 보이지도 통제되지도 않고, 그 모든 게 손가락 사이로 빠져나가는 걸 아는 기분을 당신은 모른다.

text: It is only afterward that a new idea seems reasonable. To begin with, it usually seems unreasonable.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 새로운 생각은 나중에야 합당해 보인다. 처음에는 대개 터무니없어 보인다.

text: It is the nature of science that answers automatically pose new and more subtle questions.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 답이 자동으로 더 새롭고 더 미묘한 질문을 낳는 것, 그것이 과학의 본성이다.

text: An observer studying the Solar system dispassionately, and finding himself capable of bringing the four giant planets to his notice, could reasonably say that the Solar system consisted of one star, four planets, and some traces of debris.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Outside intelligences, exploring the Solar System with true impartiality, would be quite likely to enter the Sun in their records thus: Star X, spectral class G0, 4 planets plus debris.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Predicting the future is a hopeless, thankless task, with ridicule to begin with and, all too often, scorn to end with.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 미래를 예측하는 일은 가망 없고 고마움도 못 받는 일이다. 조롱으로 시작해 대개 경멸로 끝난다.

text: Ten years on the moon could tell us more about the universe than a thousand years on the earth might be able to.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 달에서의 십 년이 지구에서의 천 년보다 우주에 대해 더 많은 것을 알려 줄 수 있다.

text: Private profit is often hidden under a careful coating of great patriotism.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Start with a planet like the earth, with a complement of simple compounds bound to exist upon it, add the energy of a nearby sun, and you are bound to end with nucleic acids. You can't avoid it.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: It is important to remember that the viciousness and wrongs of life stick out very plainly but that even at the worst times there is a great deal of goodness, kindness, and day-to-day decency that goes unnoticed and makes no headlines.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Indeed, it may well be argued that one reason for the decline in science, art, and literature was the increasing absorption of the better minds into a new sort of intellectual pursuit – theology.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: [W]hen one plays for top prizes one must be prepared to pay top stakes.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: It seems to be almost an invariable rule that as real power declines, the symbols of power multiply and intensify in compensation.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 실제 권력이 쇠퇴할수록 권력의 상징은 그 보상으로 늘어나고 강해진다. 거의 불변의 법칙처럼 보인다.

text: There is a kind of selective memory that afflicts men when they view the past. They see the good and overlook the evil.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 사람들이 과거를 볼 때 앓는 일종의 선택적 기억이 있다. 좋은 것만 보고 악한 것은 지나친다.

text: Generals are usually a conservative force who can be relied on to oppose social change.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: In the world of today can there be peace anywhere until there is peace everywhere?
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 모든 곳에 평화가 오기 전에, 오늘의 세계 어느 한 곳에 평화가 있을 수 있을까?

text: Religion is more conservative than any other aspect of human life.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 종교는 인간 삶의 어떤 영역보다도 보수적이다.

text: [N]o matter how outrageous a lie may be, it will be accepted if stated loudly enough and often enough.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: It is an odd fact that anyone who wishes to start a war must always make it appear that he is fighting in a just cause even if the real motive is naked aggression. Fortunately for the would-be aggressor, a "just cause" is very easy to find.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Probably, the most-often-repeated lesson in history is that foreigners who are called in to help one side in a civil war take over for themselves. It is a lesson that seems never to be learned despite endless repetition.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: There has never been any custom, however useless it may become with changing conditions, that isn't clung to desperately simply because it is something old and familiar.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: It is all too easy to forget that there are emotional motivations in history, as well as economic ones.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 역사에는 경제적 동기만이 아니라 감정적 동기도 있다는 사실을 잊기란 너무나 쉽다.

text: Had Hannibal had a government behind him that knew how to exploit victories – had he been born a Roman, for instance – he might have conquered the world.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: I consider one of the most important duties of any scientist the teaching of science to students and to the general public.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 나는 과학자의 가장 중요한 의무 하나가 학생과 대중에게 과학을 가르치는 일이라고 생각한다.

text: I recognize the necessity of animal experiments with my mind but not with my heart.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 동물 실험의 필요성을 나는 머리로는 인정하지만 마음으로는 인정하지 못한다.

text: Inspect every piece of pseudoscience and you will find a security blanket, a thumb to suck, a skirt to hold. What does the scientist have to offer in exchange? Uncertainty! Insecurity!
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Hypocrisy is a universal phenomenon. It ends with death, but not before.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 위선은 보편적인 현상이다. 죽음과 함께 끝날 뿐, 그 전에는 끝나지 않는다.

text: There is no belief, however foolish, that will not gather its faithful adherents who will defend it to the death.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 아무리 어리석은 믿음이라도 죽음을 무릅쓰고 지킬 신봉자를 모으지 못하는 경우는 없다.

text: Science fiction writers foresee the inevitable, and although problems and catastrophes may be inevitable, solutions are not.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Self-education is, I firmly believe, the only kind of education there is.
author: Isaac Asimov
ko: 독학이야말로 유일한 교육이라고 나는 굳게 믿는다.

text: Straightforward preaching spoils the effectiveness of a story. If you can't resist the impulse to improve your fellow human beings, do it subtly.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: [S]cientific writing is abhorrently stylized and places a premium on poor quality.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: If you're going to write a story, avoid contemporary references. They date a story and they have no staying power.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Generals are, as a matter of course, allowed to be far more idiotic than ordinary human beings are permitted to be.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: The history of science is full of revolutionary advances that required small insights that anyone might have had, but that, in fact, only one person did.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: I believe that only scientists can understand the universe. It is not so much that I have confidence in scientists being right, but that I have so much in nonscientists being wrong.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: In memory yet green, in joy still felt, The scenes of life rise sharply into view. We triumph; Life’s disasters are undealt, And while all else is old, the world is new.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: There is less trouble and trauma involved in writing a new piece than in trying to salvage an unsatisfactory old one.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: The undramatic fact is that I just think and think and think until I have something [for a story], and there is nothing marvelous or artistic about the phenomenon.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: Certain success evicts one from the paradise of winning against the odds.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: The military mind remains unparalleled as a vehicle of creative stupidity.
author: Isaac Asimov

text: [Creationists] make it sound as though a "theory" is something you dreamt up after being drunk all night.
author: Isaac Asimov
